text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has expressed serious concern over the law and order situation in Karachi and asked the Sindh province Chief Minister Liaquat Ali Jatoi to convene a high-level meeting to discuss the related issues.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto has opposed agriculture tax, saying that levies on this sector will inflate prices of essential food items.
- Union Texas Petroleum Inc will invest $250 million in Pakistan over the next three years in oil and gas exploration and production and marketing sectors.
- The United Bank Ltd has closed five of its 11 branches in Britain over the last six months in an attempt to consolidate and rationalise its operations.
- The Union Bank of Switzerland and a Pakistani brokerage house, Global Securities Ltd, have announced the setting up of a joint venture in Pakistan.
THE NEWS

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz, in a speech winding up budget debate in the National Assembly on Friday, said the government had extended the scope of a money-laundering scheme for all tax-payers, old and new, with the condition that all hidden wealth is declared before September 30.

- The opposition ended its boycott of the budget session in the National Assembly on Friday after being assured that the entire version of the verbal clash between deputy opposition leader Syed Khurshid Shah and Speaker Elahi Bakhsh Soomro would be expunged.

- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told the National Assembly on Friday that assistance of armed forces would be sought when the government holds population census in Pakistan. But he said no time had yet been set for the census.

- Some of Pakistan's nationalist and regilious political parties have criticised the Pakistani and U.S. governments for their handling of the operation to arrest Mir Aimal Kansi, who is accused of a 1993 shooting spree outside the CIA headquarters in the United States in which two CIA workers were killed and three others were injured. More than a dozen commandos, carrying submachine guns and accompanied by two men who appeared to be Americans, arrested a fair-coloured man from Shalimar hotel in Dera Ghazi Khan in the early hours of June 15 and the man whisked away could be Aimal Kansi.
- No trace of has been found of deputy opposition leader in Sindh provincial assembly Pir Mazharul Haq, who was kidnapped about two weeks ago from Hyderabad.
THE MUSLIM
- The foreign ministry of Pakistan, after the first day of second round of secretaries-level talks with India on Friday, termed the talks as "thorough and result-oriented".
- President Farooq Leghari said on Friday that Pakistan wanted India to start moving towards peace based on principles.
THE NATION

- The federal cabinet, in a meeting on Friday, voiced concern over the recent incidents of terrorism in Karachi and directed the Interior Ministry to take emergency measures in consultation with the Sindh provincial authorities.
- Five gunmen on Friday looted four million rupees from an Islamabad branch of Citibank, police and bank officials said.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
